details: Spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) experienced their worst month since inception in June, with outflows totaling $4.5 billion. This significant withdrawal of capital, including a $300 million loss from the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF in a single day, suggests a decline in institutional conviction and a worrying shift in cryptocurrency sentiment.
title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $4.5 Billion in June, Worst Month Since Debut

details: Michael Saylor's Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) introduced a "Digital Credit Capital Framework," authorizing up to $1.25 billion in Bitcoin sales and pausing new BTC purchases. The move aims to stabilize STRC pricing and increase USD reserves to $2.55 billion, marking a shift from its previous continuous accumulation strategy. While Saylor affirmed no intent to liquidate core BTC holdings, the announcement weighed on Bitcoin's price.
title: Strategy Authorizes $1.25B BTC Sales in New Capital Framework

details: The European Union's landmark Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation has fully come into force. This comprehensive regulatory framework aims to standardize crypto asset rules across the EU, offering clarity for market participants but also introducing stricter compliance requirements for crypto firms operating in the region.
title: Europe's MiCA Crypto Regulation Officially Goes Live

details: Cryptocurrency hacks and theft amounted to $75.9 million across 40 incidents in June, according to PeckShield data. Despite a decrease from May's record losses, the second quarter of 2026 is now the most hacked quarter on record, with total losses reaching approximately $775 million, highlighting persistent security vulnerabilities in the crypto space.
title: Crypto Hacks Total $76M in June, Marking Record Q2 Losses

details: Over 140 companies, including giants like Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, BlackRock, Coinbase, Ripple, Google, and Shopify, have backed the launch of Open USD (OUSD) by Open Standard. The new stablecoin offers zero-fee minting and redemption with no volume caps, and its reserve earnings are distributed back to partners, signaling a significant institutional move into crypto payments.
title: Visa, BlackRock, Coinbase Lead Open USD Stablecoin Initiative
